title: The rank of a rational matrix is at most its row count
statement: For every matrix M : Nat -> Nat -> Rat and every pair of dimensions rows, cols, Nat.Le (Rat.rank M rows cols) rows. Rat.rank M rows cols is Nat.countRange (Rat.nonzeroRowB (Rat.rowEchelon M rows cols) cols) rows -- the number of rows of the row-echelon form whose Rat.leadingIndex is strictly below cols, i.e. the number of nonzero rows. The bound follows from Nat.countRange_le alone and uses NO property of Rat.rowEchelon, of Rat.leadingIndex, or of the elementary row operations: a count of any predicate over the range [0, rows) cannot exceed rows. That is why this half of the dimension bound is free, and why the other half (rank <= cols) is not -- rank <= cols asserts that the echelon form has at most one pivot per column, which is the unproved rowEchelon_isEchelon (ADR-1554 obligation 4).

formal.statement: theorem Rat.rank_le_rows : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Rat))) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat.le (Rat.rank x0 x1 x2) x1)))

evidence.supports: `Rat.rank_le_rows` is a checked `Declaration::Theorem` with an EMPTY `Kernel::axiom_footprint` in all four preludes carrying the rationals. The `formal.statement` is the kernel's `render_lean` of the admitted type; reading it confirms the bound is against the FIRST dimension argument `x1` (the row count) and not against `x2`, which is the whole content of the claim -- the same declaration bounding rank by `x2` would be `rank_le_cols`, which is not proved here.
evidence.notes: Run 2026-09-02: prints four `found ... theorem Rat.rank_le_rows 0` rows (rat, creal, complex, cpoint) and exits 0. The checker COUNTS those rows and requires exactly 4, so a deletion, a rename, a demotion to a `Definition`, a nonzero axiom footprint, or the declaration failing to survive into a downstream prelude each make the count differ and the command exit 1. `scripts/new-fact.py` verified the pattern fails on mutated output before this file was written.

notes: ADR-0603 grading: general constructive form. Row 2 (a boundary refutation) is EMPTY BY PROOF for this family, as for ADR-1554's: the order on the constructed rationals is decidable and `Rat.nonzeroRowB` is total and `Bool`-valued, so there is no Markov-style boundary to refute. Row 3 (the decidable-fragment exact form) is the five-matrix evaluation table in `rat_prelude/rank_tests.rs`. Row 4: no import; nothing here was taken from Mathlib. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: it does not say rank <= cols, which is open and needs `rowEchelon_isEchelon` (ADR-1554 obligation 4). It does not say rank is invariant under the elementary row operations -- that is open too, and ADR-1555 records that it does NOT follow from `echelon.rs`'s three inverse laws, because those are POINTWISE and this kernel has no `funext`. It does not say `Rat.rowEchelon` computes a correct echelon form; the bound holds for ANY predicate, so it would still hold if the elimination were wrong.
